thread:
incidents-bot: ALERT — Elevated 5xx rate detected on /v1/generate (eu-west1). Rolling 5m error rate 5xx = 12.4% (baseline 0.3%). Affected model: redwood-13b-quant. Pager: #eng-oncall. See: https://metrics.redwood.ai/alerts/12345

nina: paging in, I'm oncall. Viewing dashboards now. Confirming regions/tenants impacted?

incidents-bot: Top impacted routes: /v1/generate (100%), top customer segments: EU tenants w/ dedicated routing. Error signature: 502/5xx from model-runner binary (segfault) on nodes: eu-rg-1a-{12,14,19}.

julian: I'm on runtime. I see repeated SIGSEGV in model-runner. Tail of journalctl from eu-rg-1a-12:

```
Mar 05 21:12:34 eu-rg-1a-12 model-runner[21234]: segfault at 0 ip 0x7f8b2c3... sp 0x7fff.. error 4 in model-runner[400000+1f000]
Mar 05 21:12:34 eu-rg-1a-12 kernel: [12345.678901] Code: ff 90 48 8b ...
#0  0x00007f8b2c3a1bcd in kv_cache_lookup() at kv_cache.c:234
#1  0x00007f8b2c4b2f00 in model_forward() at model.c:1120
#2  0x00007f8b2c4c3abc in worker_handle_request() at worker.c:87
```

julian: reproduces when serving long sequences > 8192 tokens; suspect KV cache boundary bug after quantized kernels.

priyanka: ops — can we triage: are we able to route EU traffic to fallback model variant? what's impact if we route to 7b or to quantized-int8 variant? need customer impact summary for SRE and CS.

cody: support — affected customers: 4 paying accounts in EU, 1 trial org. Reported increased latency and 502s. No data loss but failed inferences.

julian: mitigation proposal: 1) set routing policy to fallback model redwood-13b-quant-stable or redwood-7b-legacy for eu-west1; 2) mark problematic nodes out of rotation and restart model-runner after core dump enabled; 3) enable autoscale in eu to shift load temporarily.

nina: do it. priyanka, can you execute routing change? julian, collect coredumps and stack traces. I'll notify CS.

priyanka: running rollout command now — shifting 100% of /v1/generate eu-west1 to redwood-13b-int8-fallback.

```
# operator console command
redwoodctl routing set --route /v1/generate --region eu-west1 --to redwood-13b-int8-fallback --weight 1.0
```

priyanka: applied. Confirming traffic switch: 95% of requests now hitting fallback.

incidents-bot: Traffic shift observed. 5m 5xx rate in eu-west1 dropped to 1.1%.

julian: good. Still need to investigate root cause. Dumping cores from eu-rg-1a-12. Enabling coredump and increasing ulimit.

```
# on node
sudo sysctl -w kernel.core_pattern=/var/crash/model-runner-%e-%p.core
ulimit -c unlimited
systemctl restart model-runner
gdb -batch -ex 'thread apply all bt full' -ex quit /usr/bin/model-runner /var/crash/model-runner-model-runner-21234.core > /tmp/core-bt-21234.log
```

julian: core backtrace shows failure inside fused attention kernel after resizing KV cache: suspect off-by-one free leading to double-free in quantized path. I've opened a runtime issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/789

priyanka: nodetool — marking eu-rg-1a-12,14,19 draining and out of service to avoid further segfault cascade.

nina: CS notified: emailing affected customers and creating incident page.

cody: emailed customers, offering escalation and temporary credits. No customer wants immediate rollback; they accept fallback.

julian: patch idea: guard on KV resize boundary + add sanitizer build for quantized kernels. I'll push canary build to dedicated staging and run load tests.

nina: ok handing off to julian for investigation and root cause. I'm off in 40m. Use #incidents for updates and tag me if escalates. :round_pushpin:

julian: ack. next steps: confirm root cause, PR with fix, rehearse canary, plan controlled rollout, and postmortem. Adding labels: sev2, model-runner, segfault, eu-west1, mitigation: fallback-routing.

priyanka: closing mitigation loop. Will keep routing to fallback until patch rolled out. I'll schedule capacity increase if we see latency regressions.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — mitigation applied. 5xxs reduced to 0.8% after routing change. Monitoring for one hour before closing.

nina: thanks everyone. Great fast coordination. :clap:
